To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the solution behaviour of the hydrophobically stabilized CFZ salt forms can be manipulated in biorelevant solutions through the use of amphipathics.

amphipathatic compounds in gastrointestinal fluids can overcome the instability of clofazamine by encapsulation of clofazmine in mixed bile salt and phospholipid vesicles in the intestinal fluid, and the binding of clofazime to pepsin in gastric fluid.
the amphipathic properties of the gastrointestinal system are able to overcome the instability experienced at both low pH and high pH.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of a hydrophobic drug with amphipathic components in the gastrointestinal system.
the interactions between amphipathic molecules present in the gastrointestinal tract with the free base and salt forms of CFZ, which may influence drug absorption and bioavailability.
the effects of amphiphilic compounds in the human gastrointestinal tract on the stability of hydrophobic drugs, and the potential of this phenomenon for manipulating drug absorption.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
amphipathicity in the gastrointestinal system is an important factor in determining the solution stability of hydrophobic drugs, and thus likely has a role in influencing the rate of absorption.
the presence of amphipathics in the gastric and/or intestinal systems will increase the stability of CFZ and therefore increase its bioavailability.

the presence of bile salts, phospholipids and pepsin in biologically relevant media can significantly enhance the solution stability of clofazamine, and therefore the potential for absorption in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amphipathic nature of gastrointestinal compounds can be exploited to improve the solution stability of clofazamine, a hydrophobic drug.
the solution behaviour of hydrophobic drugs in the gastrointestinal system may be significantly influenced by the presence of endogenous amphipathic substances.
the amphipathic nature of gastrointestinal compounds can have a positive effect on the solubility of poorly water soluble drugs in biorelevant systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amphipathic nature of CFZ and the presence of amphipathics in the gastrointestinal tract may have an impact on the rate of absorption of hydrophobic drugs.
the solution stability of clofazamine in the gastrointestinal tract can be improved by the presence of amphipathics in the media.

amphipathicity in the gastrointestinal system can play a significant role in determining the solution stability of hydrophobic drugs, and that this may be an important factor in determining the rate and extent of drug absorption in vivo.
